items.followUp: List four functions of the liver and explain how it helps regulate blood glucose.

rubric.why: Bile production is one of the liver’s functions and helps with fat digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming bile production and its role in fat digestion.

rubric.why: The liver helps regulate blood glucose by storing glucose as glycogen and releasing glucose when needed.
rubric.description: Regulates blood glucose through glucose and glycogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing blood-glucose regulation through glycogen storage or release.

rubric.why: The liver deaminates excess amino acids and forms urea from nitrogenous waste.
rubric.description: Carries out deamination and forms urea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking deamination with urea formation.

rubric.why: The liver also detoxifies harmful substances, stores vitamins and iron, and breaks down worn-out red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two of detoxification, vitamin storage, iron storage, or breakdown of worn-out red blood cells.

modelAnswer: The liver produces bile, which helps in the digestion of fats.
It regulates blood glucose by converting glucose into glycogen for storage and glycogen back into glucose when needed.
It deaminates excess amino acids and forms urea from nitrogenous waste.
It breaks down worn-out red blood cells.
It helps maintain the body’s supply of nutrients through these storage and metabolic functions.

items.followUp: Compare the structure and functions of the heart, arteries and veins.

rubric.why: Arteries have thicker, more elastic walls and a narrower lumen than veins.
rubric.description: Compares the walls or lumen of arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct structural comparison of arteries and veins.

rubric.why: Veins have valves to prevent backflow; arteries generally do not.
rubric.description: Compares the presence of valves in arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the difference in valves.

accept: arteries carry blood away from the heart
veins carry blood towards the heart
arteries carry blood away from the heart
veins carry blood to the heart
rubric.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins return blood to it.
rubric.description: States the directions in which arteries and veins carry blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both directions correctly stated.

rubric.why: Capillary walls are one cell thick, allowing exchange between blood and tissues.
rubric.description: Describes capillary walls as one cell thick.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that capillary walls are one cell thick.

rubric.why: Capillaries exchange materials between the blood and body tissues.
rubric.description: Explains the exchange function of capillaries.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that capillaries exchange substances between blood and tissues.

modelAnswer: Arteries have thick, elastic walls and a relatively narrow lumen; veins have thinner walls and a wider lumen.
Arteries generally have no valves, whereas veins have valves to prevent the backward flow of blood.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry blood towards the heart.
Capillaries have extremely thin walls, only one cell thick, and connect small arteries with small veins.
Capillaries allow the exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste materials between blood and body tissues.

items.followUp: Define agriculture and name two branches of it.

rubric.why: Horticulture concerns the cultivation of garden plants, including fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining horticulture as the cultivation of garden plants or examples of them.

rubric.why: Horticulture is a specialized branch of agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that horticulture is a branch or specialized part of agriculture.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the branch of biology and agriculture concerned with cultivating garden plants, such as fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
It is related to agriculture because it is a specialized branch of agriculture.

items.followUp: Write two differences between plant and animal cells.

rubric.why: Plant cells have a cell wall, while animal cells do not.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the presence and absence of a cell wall.

rubric.why: Plant cells have chloroplasts and usually a large central vacuole; animal cells lack chloroplasts and generally have smaller vacuoles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct difference involving chloroplasts or vacuoles.

modelAnswer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside its cell membrane, whereas an animal cell has no cell wall.
Plant cells have chloroplasts and usually a large central vacuole; animal cells lack chloroplasts and generally have smaller vacuoles.
